title: Vectors

review.history: source gap; no origin or priority assertions

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. All stories and worked quantities are original constructed teaching scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate claim-level evidence before publication.
purpose: Describe displacement with signed components and separate direction from length.
meaning: A plane vector has two ordered components. Its Euclidean norm is the straight-line magnitude. Many routes can share one net vector; the zero vector has magnitude zero but no direction.

signature.angleDegrees: atan2(y,x) in degrees for a nonzero vector; null at zero

conditions: Components share compatible units and an orthonormal frame.
Norm is nonnegative and is zero exactly when both components are zero.
A norm alone does not determine the vector direction.
definition.domain_notes: The live specimen has two real components in [-5,5] and the Euclidean norm. General vectors can belong to higher-dimensional or abstract spaces; routes and other metrics are not modeled.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level reference; worked properties are author-derived for stated assumptions. Independent mathematical review pending.
